statement: Whenever the call triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r is the number of triples (i,j,k) of indices such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(nums) and the three mathematical integers nums[i], nums[j], nums[k] satisfy all three strict triangle inequalities: nums[i] + nums[j] > nums[k], nums[i] + nums[k] > nums[j], and nums[j] + nums[k] > nums[i]. Equivalently, r = |{ (i,j,k) : 0 <= i < j < k < len(nums) and the three displayed inequalities hold }|.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the call triangle_number(nums) returns a result; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Let p be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > 0. Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r <= p*(p-1)*(p-2)/6, which is C(p,3) with the convention that this value is 0 when p < 3.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 2 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r = 1 if nums[0] + nums[1] > nums[2] and nums[0] + nums[2] > nums[1] and nums[1] + nums[2] > nums[0], and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) = 3 and for every i with 0 <= i < 3, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r = len(nums)*(len(nums)-1)*(len(nums)-2)/6, which equals C(len(nums),3) and is 0 when len(nums) < 3.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 1000, and there exists an integer c with 1 <= c <= 1000 such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Let m be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 1. Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r = m*(m-1)*(m-2)/6, which equals C(m,3) and is 0 when m < 3.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = 0 or nums[i] = 1.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns r and triangle_number(nums') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Both nums and nums' satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(nums) = len(nums') <= 1000 and all entries are between 0 and 1000. There exists a bijection p from {0,...,len(nums)-1} to itself such that nums'[i] = nums[p(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns r and triangle_number(nums') returns r', r' = r + q, where q is the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n such that nums[i] + nums[j] > x, nums[i] + x > nums[j], and nums[j] + x > nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). We have 1 <= n <= 999, len(nums') = n+1, nums'[i] = nums[i] for every 0 <= i < n, nums'[n] = x, and all entries of nums and nums' are between 0 and 1000.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, r = |{ (i,j,k) : 0 <= i < j < k < len(b) and b[i] + b[j] > b[k] }|. For nondecreasing nonnegative b, a triple i<j<k satisfies all three strict triangle inequalities exactly when b[i] + b[j] > b[k].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; b is a nondecreasing reordering of nums.

statement: Whenever triangle_number(nums) returns a result r, every counted index triple (i,j,k) has nums[i] > 0, nums[j] > 0, and nums[k] > 0. Consequently, if at most two entries of nums are positive, r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.
